title: Florida House, District 90
what_it_does: Represents District 90 (Part of Palm Beach) in the Florida House; votes on state laws and the state budget.
verified_ballot_note: Candidate list taken from the Florida Division of Elections, 2026 general election candidate list on 2026-09-18 (https://dos.elections.myflorida.com/candidates/CanList.asp); statuses Qualified/Unopposed only. Counties from the Legislature's district listings.

candidates.name: Ionel Roiban
candidates.background: Ionel Roiban is a software and AI engineer who has lived in Boynton Beach for 25 years and is running for office for the first time. He describes himself as a private-sector outsider running a data-driven campaign focused on affordability and local issues rather than national politics.

roster_sources.title: Florida Division of Elections, 2026 general election candidate list

property_tax.summary: His site says he backs Amendment 3 and would help write its implementing law, and supports phasing out non-school property taxes on homesteads; he says he is voting yes.
property_tax.quote: I'm voting yes — and asking for a seat in the majority that writes the implementing law.

candidates.name: Rob Long
candidates.occupation: Civil engineer; former Delray Beach city commissioner; state representative since December 2025
candidates.background: Rob Long is a civil engineer with a degree from Penn State and an MBA from the University of Florida. He served on the Delray Beach City Commission and as an elected Palm Beach Soil & Water Conservation District supervisor, and founded a grassroots engagement firm. He won a December 2025 special election for District 90 and is seeking a full term.

roster_sources.title: Florida Division of Elections, 2026 general election candidate list

property_tax.summary: He voted no on HJR 203 (Feb. 19, 2026), his site opposes the governor's property tax amendment as shifting costs to renters and small businesses, and he called the amendment a 'shell game' in August 2026. He did not vote on HJR 1-F.
property_tax.quote: The governor is going to blow a hole in your city or county's budget and then blame the city or county for trying to patch it up.

housing.summary: Supports fully funding the state housing trust funds, expanding SHIP and SAIL, using public land for workforce housing and down-payment assistance, and giving local governments flexibility to add housing.
housing.quote: I support fully funding Florida’s housing trust funds, expanding SHIP and SAIL, using appropriate public land for workforce housing, and helping first-time buyers with down-payment assistance.

abortion.summary: Opposes Florida's six-week abortion ban and supports restoring protections like those under Roe v. Wade, including access before viability.
abortion.quote: I oppose Florida’s six-week abortion ban and support restoring protections consistent with Roe v. Wade, including access before viability

growth.summary: Says Florida has moved too far toward state preemption and supports a stronger presumption in favor of local home rule over local decisions.
growth.quote: I support a stronger presumption in favor of home rule and limiting preemption to cases where there is a clear statewide interest rather than using it as a one-size-fits-all political tool.

healthcare.summary: Says the state should use every available tool to keep people insured, including maximizing federal Medicaid dollars and protecting coverage; he does not explicitly call for Medicaid expansion.
healthcare.quote: Florida should use every available tool to keep people insured and protect access to care.

insurance.summary: Wants lower premiums through competition, mitigation programs, transparency and consumer protections, without leaving taxpayers holding the risk; he does not call for rate caps or a larger Citizens.
insurance.quote: Florida should focus on bringing down insurance premiums through stronger competition, mitigation and resilience programs, transparency, consumer protections, and reforms that make the market more stable without leaving taxpayers holding the risk.

elections.summary: Voted no on CS/CS/HB 991 when it passed the House on Feb. 25, 2026 and no on final House passage March 12, 2026. CS/CS/HB 991 (2026), now law (Ch. 2026-26), requires the state to verify voters' U.S. citizenship using driver-license and other government records and removes student and retirement-home IDs from the IDs accepted at the polls. On VOTE411 he said he opposes unnecessary barriers to voting and that required documents should be free.
elections.quote: I oppose creating unnecessary barriers to voting
